title: The Big Show of 1951: Sarah, Nat King Cole and closing spots
summary: On the first big package show, with the Ellington band, George Treadwell made Sarah late to test her closing slot, and Nat Cole proved the heavyweight.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And then we can start the second half of the show. And there was another time, in what we called the Big Show of '51, which was the first big package show, this was with the Ellington Band. Oh, we had the Marie Bryant Dancers and Peg Leg Bates, Stumpy and Stumpy, Patterson and Jackson, Jimmy Rodgers, Nat Cole, and we were going into Pittsburgh. Now, normally Sarah had what was called the choice spots. She'd close the first half. There's no pressure there. Nat Cole was the only one, King Cole was the only one that could close the second half of the show. And at that time George Treadwell, who was a trumpet player, that was Sarah's manager.

And husband, yes, made her late on purpose, to see if she could hold up closing the second half. That meant that if she was absent Nat would have to close the first half. Well, he learned his lesson. As much as I admire Sarah, Nat King Cole was a complete heavyweight.
Just as -- he could walk on stage, address the stage, and he was in business.
